data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim asserts resumption 'is safe only if the system emitted an explicit barrier or suspend event' — a necessary condition. But its own counterconditions identify two rival criteria (stateless self-contained events, and full-state checkpointing on every event) under which no barrier is needed and resumption is safe. The problem demands adjudication between rival criteria to determine 'exactly when' resumption is safe vs. refused. SRC_001 never reconciles the barrier gate with these alternatives: it presents a single universal necessary condition while simultaneously conceding it is unnecessary in acknowledged-safe cases. For a stateless system interrupted after a complete event with no barrier emitted, the main claim says 'must refuse' while the countercondition says 'safe' — a direct contradiction that prevents the target from determining exactly when resumption is permitted.
